message.content:
**Hydrogen (H)** – the simplest and most abundant element in the universe.

| Property | Value / Description |
|----------|---------------------|
| **Atomic number** | 1 |
| **Atomic mass** | 1.008 u (average; protium ≈ 1.0079 u) |
| **Electron configuration** | 1s¹ |
| **Isotopes** | Protium (¹H, stable), Deuterium (²H, stable, 1 p + 1 n), Tritium (³H, radioactive, β⁻‑decay, t½ ≈ 12.3 y) |
| **Electronegativity (Pauling)** | 2.20 |
| **First ionization energy** | 13.598 eV (1312 kJ mol⁻¹) |
| **Electron affinity** | 72.8 kJ mol⁻¹ |
| **Covalent radius** | 31 pm |
| **Van der Waals radius** | 120 pm |
| **Melting point** | –259.16 °C (14 K) |
| **Boiling point** | –252.87 °C (20.28 K) |
| **Density at STP** | 0.08988 g L⁻¹ |
| **Molar volume at STP** | 22.414 L mol⁻¹ |
| **State at room temperature** | Colorless, odorless, tasteless gas |
| **Flammability** | Extremely flammable; forms explosive mixtures with air (range 4–75 % H₂ in air) |
| **Reactivity** | Forms hydrides with metals (e.g., NaH, CaH₂), reacts with halogens (HX), oxidizes to water or oxides (H₂O, H₂O₂) |
| **Bonding** | Diatomic molecule (H₂) with a single covalent bond; H₂ is a non‑polar, weakly interacting gas (low boiling point). |
| **Spectral lines** | Lyman series (UV), Balmer series (visible), Paschen series (IR) – classic hydrogen spectrum. |
| **Role in stars** | Core fusion product (proton‑proton chain, CNO cycle) → helium; also fuels stellar winds and contributes to interstellar chemistry. |
| **Applications** | Fuel (hydrogen fuel cells), reducing agent (steelmaking), laboratory reagent (reducing metal salts), cryogenics (liquid H₂ as coolant). |

These values give a comprehensive snapshot of hydrogen’s physical, chemical, and nuclear characteristics.
